title: Page Industries nears 52-week low as weak sales growth spooks investors
summary: Page Industries has witnessed a sharp decline in its share prices, approaching a 52-week low, driven by disappointing sales volume growth. Analysts are growing wary about the company's prospects for achieving double-digit volume increases for FY27, especially with current trends. The operating margin has slipped to 20.8% due to rising input costs.

title: Select HFCs offer rate cuts, top-ups to retain borrowers
summary: As competition among lenders intensifies, housing finance firms are deploying a range of tactics to secure their customer base. These include attractive interest rate discounts and personalized offers designed to minimize mortgage transfers. Home First Finance is witnessing a drop in balance-transfer outflows as a result of these strategic actions. However, despite improved retention through analytics-driven methods, the industry faces ongoing significant net balance-transfer outflows each month.

title: Sensex surges 20% in dollar terms as foreign money chases India
summary: The Sensex has increased by 20% in dollar terms this quarter, marking a potential bull market. Foreign fund flows have contributed significantly to this surge, driven by global investors seeking diversification. The rupee's appreciation has also enhanced returns for foreign investors holding Indian assets. Despite recent gains, many investors remain cautious and have yet to fully engage in the Indian market.

title: D-Street poised for a gap-up start as GIFT Nifty trades firmly higher
summary: Indian stock markets experienced a robust upswing on Friday, driven by a surge in domestic purchases against a backdrop of weaker global trends. The banking sector emerged as a key player, pushing weekly gains to 5.9%. Market experts foresee the Nifty index climbing towards record highs, likely crossing the 25500 mark, with this level serving as a potential support point.

title: Stocks in news: Adani Energy, Maruti Suzuki, RailTel, Waaree Energies and Indian Bank
summary: Indian equity benchmarks ended higher on Friday, driven by a rally in private banking stocks. The Nifty 50 index rose by 286 points, approaching a critical technical resistance level. Adani Energy Solutions, Maruti Suzuki India, and several other companies are expected to be in focus on Monday. Key developments include share acquisitions, price increases, and capital-raising plans from various firms.

title: Nifty eyes 26,300 as analysts favour banking, auto and realty stocks
summary: Analysts anticipate a continued upward trend for the Nifty index, targeting levels around 26,000 to 26,300. Recommended strategies include buying on dips while being cautious due to overbought indicators. Key stocks include Federal Bank, Apollo Hospitals, and HDFC Life, among others. The Bank Nifty remains a favored investment due to its relative strength and momentum. Investors are advised to favor large-cap stocks amidst selective participation in the market.

title: FPIs turn aggressive buyers, invest Rs 1.18 lakh crore into Indian equities in November
summary: Foreign portfolio investors have become net buyers of Indian equities, making substantial investments in November. They have invested over ₹1.18 lakh crore so far, indicating a strong market reversal. Previously, FPIs were net sellers, offloading equities worth around ₹5.51 lakh crore from October 2024 to mid-October 2026. The recent buying trend has occurred over 13 consecutive trading sessions, averaging around ₹1,450 crore per hour.

title: Chandrasekaran to push Tata Sons IPO plan at board meet, company valued at up to Rs 18 lakh crore
summary: Tata Sons is working on a public listing plan that may value the holding company at ₹18 lakh crore. Chairman N Chandrasekaran will present the IPO proposal at the upcoming board meeting. This move follows the Reserve Bank of India's directive for a listing without delay due to existing regulatory requirements. Investment banks, including Bank of America, are involved in the IPO process preparations.

title: Mahindra Finance scouts gold loan firms for acquisition, evaluates four potential targets
summary: Mahindra & Mahindra Financial Services is exploring acquisitions of gold finance companies to diversify its revenue streams. Among the targets are Indel Money, Kosamattam Finance, ICL Fincorp, and Supra Pacific Financial Services. Discussions have begun, but no formal offers have been made at this stage. The company aims to increase its presence in the growing gold loan market while maintaining its vehicle financing operations.

title: Stock Radar: Bharti Airtel rallies 14% in a month; multi-month triangle breakout signals further upside
summary: Bharti Airtel has broken out of a multi-month triangle pattern on the weekly charts, signalling further upside potential. The stock has rebounded sharply after finding support above Rs 1,700 in September and is nearing fresh record highs. Experts recommend medium-term buying, with a target of Rs 2,400 over the next 3-4 months.

title: Banks warn higher costs could hit demand as RBI weighs further repo hike
summary: Bank executives held consultations with Reserve Bank of India officials regarding inflation risks and capital formation challenges. They expressed concern that higher interest rates may affect consumption demand due to rising costs. Particular attention was given to stress in sectors such as agriculture and gold loans. India's gold loan market saw non-performing assets rise significantly in recent months.

title: Tata Steel clears sale of two units to APL Apollo
summary: Tata Steel has decided to sell its tubes business and Tata Steel Colours in two transactions valued at ₹28,000 crore. APL Apollo Tubes will acquire the tubes unit and Tata Steel Colours, with completion expected by March 31, 2028. The tubes unit generated a turnover of approximately ₹11,375 crore while Tata Steel Colours reported around ₹4,680 crore in revenue.

summary: US Treasury futures declined as demand for havens waned on signs that the recent selloff in equities may be drawing some buyers back.

Global technology shares sold off sharply, while inflation, upcoming RBI policy and GDP data may keep domestic markets cautious.
